item.title: Poor financial records, cash flow woes crippling Nigerian businesses — SWAN
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Society of Women Accountants of Nigeria (SWAN) has identified poor financial record-keeping, inadequate cash flow management, ineffective pricing and limited understanding of profitability as some of the factors undermining the survival and growth of businesses in Nigeria. The association said many promising businesses struggle not necessarily because of a lack of opportunities or customers, but because their owners lack the financial knowledge required to manage resources and make informed decisions. SWAN stated this at its 2026 Accounting for Non-Accountants Workshop, held on Thursday at the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) Annex, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. The workshop, organised as part of the association’s Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives, had the theme, “Business Made Easy: Practical Financial Skills.” Speaking at the event, Chairperson of the Planning Committee, Mrs Ruth Jawo, said financial literacy had become essential for entrepreneurs, traders, professionals, employees and business managers, particularly amid the country’s challenging economic conditions. According to her, financial knowledge would enable business owners to make informed decisions, manage resources effectively, avoid penalties and achieve sustainable growth. “The theme reflects SWAN’s commitment to simplifying financial concepts and equipping participants with practical knowledge,” she said. item.description: By Elizabeth Onyogha Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) WKND 2026 opened in Lagos yesterday, bringing together leading creatives, investors, policymakers, business leaders and cultural figures from across Africa and the diaspora to explore investment, financing and commercial opportunities in the continent’s creative economy. item.description: By Udeme Akpan The Rural Electrification Agency (REA) has flagged off the development of 37 mini-grid projects with a combined solar generation capacity of approximately 18.8 megawatts-peak (MWp) in Zamfara State. item.title: Don’t allow yourself be used to stifle democracy, NDC to Judiciary
item.description: By Henry Umoru The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has urged the judiciary not to allow itself to be used to stifle the nation’s democracy. The party has cautioned the judiciary to guard its independence, impartiality, and integrity at all times. The NDC said while it respects the judiciary as the last hope of the common man, it is concerned as a party that judgments of this nature, if not carefully handled, would at the end of the day risk creating the impression that the courts are being used to scuttle democracy and weaken opposition. In a statement signed late Thursday night by the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, he said the way and manner some of these judgements are being churned out, especially from the High Courts suggests a deliberate effort to shut out the ADC from the forthcoming general elections by other means. According to Director, if not checked, this would amount to further shrinking the chances of multi-party democracy which is already under a big threat under the APC-led government of President Bola Tinubu. item.title: 2027: Tinubu, T. Y. Danjuma, Northeast, North-Central leaders meet in Aso Villa
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru Ahead of January 16, 2027 presidential election, the former Minister of Defence, General Theophilus Danjuma (retd) and political leaders from the Northeast and North-Central geopolitical zones yesterday, met behind closed doors with President Bola Tinubu at the Aso Villa, Abuja. The meeting it was gathered was part of have consultations aimed at mobilising support for the President. The meeting focused on forging political cooperation, security and other issues affecting their communities, just as the visitors said there have been remarkable improvements in security and the administration’s contributions to the development of their communities. The delegation was made up of the Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang; his Taraba State counterpart, Agbu Kefas; former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Yakubu Dogara; Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd); and National Chairman of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentanwe Yilwatda. Speaking with journalists after the meeting, Dogara disclosed that the delegation visited the President to express solidarity with his administration and explore strategies for strengthening political support for him across their communities. He said the consultations were particularly significant as political activities gathered momentum ahead of the next general elections. He said the consultations were particularly significant as political activities gathered momentum ahead of the next general elections. item.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League as Milan lose again
item.description: Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches. Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty. Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes. Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth’s substitutes sent the European newcomers top of the table with a fourth successive victory. Marco Rose’s side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend. “It’s a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp,” Rose told TNT Sports. “It’s up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble.” Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe. Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off. “We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight,” Amorim told Sky Sport. “I don’t want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance.” Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase. “I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting,” Amorim added. Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time. Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage’s struggling side. Palace, last season’s UEFA Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League’s relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference. item.title: Ebola patient flown to UK from DR Congo
item.description: A UK medic who tested positive for Ebola while working on the outbreak of the disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown to London for treatment, the government said Thursday. The unnamed British citizen “has returned to the UK for specialist treatment after testing positive for the disease”, the government said in a statement. Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. The British government said that the UK medic is now being treated at the Royal Free Hospital in London. This hospital has a high-level isolation unit “specifically designed for this purpose” and strict protocols to prevent contact with the general public, it said. Renu Bindra, deputy director of the all hazards public health response team at the UK health security agency (UKHSA) said “the risk to the wider public remains low”. Last month, Nigeria reported an Ebola case involving a 42-year-old Swiss woman whose husband works at the country’s embassy. She was flown for treatment in Geneva. item.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
item.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” Oshiomhole said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. item.title: ADC Court Ruling: ‘APC Afraid Of Strong Candidate Against Tinubu’ – Osunbor
item.description: A former Governor of Edo State and National Legal Adviser of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Oserheimen Osunbor, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being jittery ahead of the January 2027 presidential election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Osunbor said the APC did not want a strong candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “I have said that repeatedly, they (APC) are afraid of any strong candidate running against President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election,” Osunbor said. ﻿ The ADC legal adviser said the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, were continuing with their campaigns because they believed the court judgment nullifying Atiku’s candidacy would not stand. “Our presidential candidate (Atiku Abubakar) and the presidential campaign is going on, unperturbed because we believe that this judgment will not stand and cannot stand,” he said. Osunbor said the party would appeal the judgment to ensure that a higher court sets it aside. He expressed optimism that Atiku would survive the current challenge, insisting that the former Vice President had the support of the people. “Atiku will survive because the people are behind him. The force of the people will be greater than the force of those who want to enslave Nigerians,” he said. Osunbor’s comments followed Thursday’s judgment by the Federal High Court in Abuja, which sacked the David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated actions taken by the party under the leadership, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate for the 2027 election. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the ADC. The party has rejected the ruling and vowed to challenge it at the appellate court. item.title: Traders attack Edo Consumer Protection Committee members over fake products
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu – BENIN CITY Member of the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee led by its chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu were, on Thursday, attacked by some beverage sellers while trying to enforce ban on sales of fake, adulterated and unauthorised drinks along Mission Road in Benin City, the state capital. He said the government was strengthening border security and expanding bilateral, regional and international defence cooperation through intelligence sharing, specialised training and technological support. Musa added that Nigeria continued to maintain security relationships with Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali despite their withdrawal from ECOWAS, including military training and cooperation around border areas. He warned that instability in the Sahel posed a serious threat to West Africa and urged regional countries to work together to prevent the collapse of neighbouring states. The minister also highlighted the importance of local defence manufacturing, disclosing that the government had strengthened the country’s defence industry through legislative reforms and partnerships with equipment manufacturers. He said Nigeria recently hosted the first African International Military Defence Exhibition, which attracted 63 countries and provided opportunities for local manufacturers to meet international partners and sign investment agreements. According to him, domestic production of military equipment would reduce dependence on foreign suppliers, create employment and generate foreign exchange. He called on Nigerians with expertise in cybersecurity, drone manufacturing and other defence technologies to bring forward their ideas for possible collaboration with the Defence Industry Corporation of Nigeria. Addressing concerns about the increasing involvement of the military in internal security operations, Musa acknowledged that soldiers had become overstretched by prolonged deployments across the country. He said the military’s involvement was necessary in situations where security challenges exceeded the capacity of the police but stressed that the armed forces were working to strengthen police capacity to enable soldiers to gradually return to their primary responsibilities. According to him, the military was already assisting the police while the government pursued additional recruitment, equipment procurement and institutional reforms. He disclosed that security agencies were enjoying unprecedented cooperation, describing the current level of interagency coordination as a significant improvement. Musa also highlighted the role of communities in combating insecurity, urging Nigerians to report suspicious activities rather than remain indifferent. He said criminals often operated within communities and depended on local support, adding that security agencies could not succeed without the cooperation of citizens. The minister cited community-based intelligence and the use of civilian joint task forces as important components of the security strategy, noting that local residents could provide timely information to security operatives. He also disclosed that the military was working with forest rangers and other community-based security structures to protect farmers and enable agricultural activities to continue in vulnerable areas. On the welfare of military personnel, the minister said the government had increased soldiers’ salaries and was improving their living conditions, healthcare and operational support. He recalled that a private soldier previously earned about ₦49,000 monthly before the amount was increased to approximately ₦100,000 and subsequently to nearly ₦200,000. He said military personnel and their families were entitled to free medical treatment, adding that soldiers requiring specialised treatment could be flown abroad. Musa also explained that military personnel underwent psychological preparation before deployment and assessment after operations to address the effects of traumatic experiences. He said returning soldiers were monitored for psychological challenges, including post-traumatic stress disorder, anger and other behavioural changes. According to him, military personnel could undergo two to three weeks of post-deployment assessment and support before returning to their families and units. He added that the military provided support systems for soldiers’ spouses and families, including access to loans, medical care and educational assistance for their children. item.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
item.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. item.title: 2027 UTME: JAMB moves to shut down substandard CBT centres
item.description: By Joseph Erunke The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME), warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed. According to a post on the Board’s official X handle on Thursday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. Reiterating its position, JAMB declared that accreditation would not be automatic for CBT centres seeking to participate in the exercise. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment. The strict accreditation regime is also expected to address operational shortcomings that have historically threatened the smooth conduct of computer-based examinations, including inadequate facilities and poor technical readiness. With preparations for the 2027 UTME gathering momentum, the Board maintained that compliance with its accreditation requirements would remain non-negotiable for all CBT centres seeking approval to participate in the nationwide examination. item.title: British woman, unborn baby die in Nigeria; family seeks help to bring bodies home
item.description: A 40-year-old British woman who relocated to Nigeria to start a new life with her husband has died alongside her unborn baby after developing sepsis. Claire Chadwick, who was 37 weeks pregnant, reportedly suffered septic shock after her baby girl died in the womb. In a report by Daily Mail UK, Chadwick had moved to Nigeria to be with her husband, Ibrahim, and was expecting their first child together. She had built a social media following of thousands through videos documenting their relationship, religious beliefs and food challenges on TikTok and Instagram. Her death has left her family devastated, with her sister, Shannon, revealing that she is survived by her 19-year-old son in Wales, her husband and other relatives. Describing her late sister, Shannon said Claire was a funny and fiercely strong-minded woman who lived life on her own terms. “She was a woman who lived her life in her own way and she will leave a lasting impression on everyone who knew her,” she told WalesOnline. The family has since launched a GoFundMe campaign with a target of £10,000 to repatriate Claire and her unborn daughter to the United Kingdom for burial. Explaining the purpose of the fundraiser, Shannon said the family wanted to bring both bodies home so they could be laid to rest with dignity and surrounded by their loved ones. “More than anything, we want them both returned so they can be laid to rest with dignity, surrounded by the family who love them,” she said. The fundraiser has attracted widespread support, with Shannon describing the response as overwhelming. She also expressed gratitude to REST, a charity that supports families dealing with the sudden or tragic deaths of loved ones abroad. Tributes have also poured in from friends and well-wishers, who remembered Chadwick as a kind, caring and cheerful woman. One supporter recalled knowing her from childhood and described her as lovely, while another said she was devastated by the loss, remembering her as someone who always made people laugh. The family hopes to raise enough money to bring Claire and her unborn daughter back to the UK. item.title: Zidane’s son dropped from Algeria squad for AFCON qualifiers
item.description: Algeria goalkeeper Luca Zidane was left out of the national team squad on Thursday ahead of two Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Togo, coach Brahim Hemdani said. Zidane, 28, has recently been missing from the Algerian team, owing to injury and a two-game suspension over scuffles during an AFCON game against Nigeria in January. But his exclusion was “based on sporting criteria”, Hemdani told journalists. “I need to have three goalkeepers who were getting as much playing time as possible.” Hemdani called up USM Alger goalkeeper Oussama Benbot alongside Melvin Mastil of Swiss club Lausanne-Sport and Abdelatif Ramdane of MC Alger. Zidane, a son of French football icon Zinedine Zidane, joined the Fennecs after changing his sporting nationality in September 2025 to represent Algeria, where his family has roots. The Leganes goalkeeper’s absence came as a surprise, along with that of Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri. Ait-Nouri had been sent home in September following a reported dispute with the coaching staff during a match against Zambia. But Hemdani said there had been “no problem” after his choice not to include the left-back in his next 26-man squad, adding that there were “criteria for inclusion”. “However, anything is possible in the future, and no one has been permanently excluded,” the coach said. Algeria are set to face Togo on November 14 and 17. They have four points from two games and are currently top of AFCON qualification Group I, which includes Zambia and Burundi. item.title: Nigerian teenager, Fawaz jailed four years for attempting to steal Porsche in London
item.description: A 19-year-old Nigerian teenager, Fawaz Oyedeji, has been sentenced to four years in prison in the United Kingdom for attempting to steal a £72,500 Porsche Cayenne using an imitation firearm. Oyedeji, who is from Greenwich, London, posed as a prospective buyer after responding to an online advertisement for the luxury sports utility vehicle. He arranged to meet the seller at the victim’s home in Southwark on Tuesday, March 18, to inspect the vehicle. After the victim showed him around the Porsche, the pair entered the front seats to discuss the sale. Oyedeji then produced what appeared to be a firearm, pointed it at the seller and demanded the car keys. However, the victim resisted and fought back, forcing Oyedeji to abandon the attempt and flee from the scene. The police were subsequently alerted and launched an investigation into the incident. Detectives traced the phone used to arrange the vehicle inspection to Oyedeji, establishing that it had been in the vicinity of both his home address and the scene of the attempted robbery. Investigators also obtained CCTV footage showing his movements shortly before and after the incident. Clothing matching what the suspect wore during the attempted robbery was also recovered by officers. Oyedeji was arrested at his home on Leonard Robbins Path within 38 hours of the offence. item.title: 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has dismissed the political support behind Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the wave that propelled him in the 2023 election no longer exists. Wike also described Obi as a dramatist, insisting that the former Anambra State governor had nothing to offer Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. The minister spoke on Thursday during his monthly media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he questioned the prospects of the NDC presidential ticket featuring Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. “All this so-called Obi kererenke doesn’t exist again. I have killed it,” Wike said. He argued that the political circumstances that helped Obi secure significant support in the 2023 presidential election had changed. “Nigerians know that Obi has nothing to offer, he is a dramatist. You were there when Soludo exposed him,” the minister said. Wike also criticised the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, saying Nigerians had already given him and other politicians opportunities to govern. “Nigerians know that Atiku and co have been given the opportunity, but they did not do anything. Nigerians know that the former governor of Rivers State looted our state,” he said. The FCT minister acknowledged Kwankwaso’s popularity but questioned whether his political influence extended beyond Kano State, where he won the 2023 presidential election. “I agree that Kwankwaso is very popular, but he ran in 2023 and won in Kano, fine, but what about the other northern states? What about the North-Central, what will happen there?” he asked. item.title: Atiku Takes Presidential Campaign To Kebbi, Pledges To Restore Fuel Subsidy
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to restore fuel subsidy, improve security and create employment if elected president in 2027. Atiku made the pledge on Thursday during a campaign rally in Kebbi State, where he called on voters to support the ADC, describing it as the only party committed to addressing the three issues. “The people of Kebbi State, let me ask you a few questions. Do you want the return of subsidy? Do you want security? Do you want employment? Therefore you have no option other than the ADC. ADC is the only political party that is committed to these three objectives and more to bring about prosperity, unity and peace to the people of our country,” he said. The former Vice President and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the President Bola Tinubu administration, describing them as legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. Supporters of the ADC gathered at the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party faithful for what he described as their resistance to intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 general elections would be a referendum between suffering Nigerians and the Federal Government under President Tinubu. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that no amount of intimidation could stop. He called on the people of Kebbi State to vote for Atiku as president, Abubakar Malami as governor and other ADC candidates in the 2027 general elections. The rally ended with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Crowd at Atiku Abubakar’s presidential campaign rally in Kebbi. The campaign in Kebbi came hours after a Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the leadership of the Senator David Mark-led ADC and voided the actions taken by the party’s executives, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku rejected the ruling, describing it as an attempt to weaken his political support and frustrate his campaign. He said he would challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The ADC also rejected the decision, accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to cripple the opposition and vowing to challenge the judgment through all available judicial processes.
